title: Qwen3-VL-235B grounding accuracy degrades in vLLM 0.11.1 and later on Hopper GPUs
body: I'm seeing degraded grounding accuracy with Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct on vLLM 0.11.1 and later. My environment is Ubuntu 22.04 with PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129, Python 3.12, and 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs. Grounding examples and environment details are attached.

symptoms_visible: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct returns inaccurate grounding locations on vLLM 0.11.1 and later in my 8×H20 environment.
N0.label: N0 grounding degradation reported

symptoms_visible: Grounding boxes are inaccurate with the default Flash Attention backend on Hopper systems, while an A100 comparison produces an accurate location.
N1.label: N1 backend and hardware scope collected

symptoms_visible: The inaccurate grounding result is unchanged when the multimodal encoder uses TORCH_SDPA and when the smaller model is run on one H100 without tensor parallelism.
N2.label: N2 encoder backend and tensor parallelism ruled out

symptoms_visible: With --enforce-eager, the grounding locations are accurate again on vLLM 0.11.1 and 0.11.2, but inference is significantly slower.
N3.label: N3 eager execution probe restores accuracy

symptoms_visible: Affected operators report accurate grounding after either downgrading Triton from 3.5.0 to 3.4.0 or rebuilding Triton 3.5 with the identified compiler correction; I have not yet reported my own retest result.
N4.label: N4 corrected Triton builds verified by other affected operators

symptoms_visible: Grounding output is accurate in affected operators' environments after installing a Triton build without the faulty compiled-kernel behavior; my own updated environment has not yet been retested in the thread.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix established but reporter verification pending

question_patterns: Which attention backend is logged when the server starts?
Can you paste the startup line identifying the attention backend?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My startup log says that I'm using the Flash Attention backend on the V1 engine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm using a different supported backend, and switching to Flash Attention makes the grounding accurate.
The startup line spells the backend as FLASH_ATTN, but it is still the default backend on the V1 engine.

question_patterns: Does this reproduce on Hopper GPUs, and do you have a comparison from another GPU architecture?
Can you compare the same grounding prompt on H20 or H100 and A100 hardware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I reproduce the degradation on Hopper hardware, including H20, H100 and H200 systems. With the same Wikipedia login-button prompt, the H100 or H200 output is misplaced while the A100 output identifies the button correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same prompt is equally inaccurate on A100 and Hopper, and the outputs do not differ by GPU architecture.
I reproduce it on H100 rather than H20, while the A100 comparison remains accurate.

edges.comment: Thread c0, c2-c10: the reporter supplied the H20 and backend facts; participant1 and participant5 supplied the H100/H200 versus A100 comparison. These affected users are folded into one simulated user side, without importing the unrelated H20 decode-performance complaint from c5.

question_patterns: Could you launch with --mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA and report whether the grounding changes?
Please test the multimodal encoder with TORCH_SDPA and compare the result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There is no change with --mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA. The grounding result is the same as before.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: TORCH_SDPA makes the grounding accurate while the default multimodal encoder backend remains inaccurate.

question_patterns: Can you test without tensor parallelism to determine whether tensor partitioning causes the error?
Please run a model that fits on one Hopper GPU with tensor-parallel-size 1 and compare its grounding.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking on one H100 with --tensor-parallel-size 1 and --pipeline-parallel-size 1. The result was still the same.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The one-GPU run is accurate, and the grounding error only appears with tensor parallelism enabled.

edges.comment: Thread c12-c14, participant1's system: both handler-initiated configuration probes are measurements. Their raw outcomes rule out the encoder-attention selection and tensor-parallel partitioning without placing an engineer diagnosis in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you run the same grounding request with --enforce-eager and report both accuracy and performance?
Please compare the same prompt with eager execution enabled and disabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Adding --enforce-eager restores the grounding accuracy on both vLLM 0.11.1 and 0.11.2 for my Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8 deployment. The boxes look correct again, but model inference becomes significantly slower.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The grounding remains inaccurate with --enforce-eager, with the same displaced boxes as the default run.
Eager execution restores accuracy but is only moderately slower in my workload.

edges.comment: Thread c15-c20: participant7 first demonstrated an accurate eager run, participant1 reproduced it, and the reporter confirmed it on the 235B FP8 deployment while reporting the speed penalty. This is a configuration probe and temporary workaround, so it remains a clarification-only measurement. The later maintainer conclusion that torch.compile rather than CUDA-graph capture is responsible is not put in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you test the alternate dependency version suggested in the debugging discussion and rerun the same grounding example?
Please try the proposed dependency-version comparison in a separate environment and report only whether the boxes change.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I downgraded Triton from 3.5.0 to 3.4.0 and the grounding accuracy was restored.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Grounding is still inaccurate with Triton 3.4.0, including under the same prompt and image.

question_patterns: Can you install the provided test wheel and rerun the same grounding example?
Please test the custom dependency build that was shared in the thread and report whether the output boxes change.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebuilt Triton 3.5 with triton-lang/triton#9035 cherry-picked, and it fixed the issue. This was confirmed with vLLM 0.13.0 and 0.14.0 images.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The rebuilt Triton produces the same inaccurate boxes as the stock Triton package.
The custom build restores accuracy on vLLM 0.14.0, but I did not also test 0.13.0.

edges.comment: Thread c25, c30, c34-c35: participant9 reported the Triton 3.4.0 result, while participant12 and participant13 confirmed rebuilt Triton 3.5 packages. These are pre-solution tests by other affected operators folded into the user side. The original reporter only said they would try the downgrade and never posted their own result.

solution.intent: Replace the affected torch.compile/Inductor Triton code generation path with a corrected Triton build: temporarily use Triton 3.4.0 or rebuild the compatible Triton release with the upstream compiler correction, then verify the same grounding examples before declaring the reporter's deployment resolved.
solution.concrete_example: In a compatible test environment, either pin Triton 3.4.0 or install a Triton 3.5 build containing the confirmed compiler correction, restart vLLM without relying on --enforce-eager, and rerun the exact images and prompts that produced displaced boxes. Keep --enforce-eager only as a temporary diagnostic workaround because of its inference-speed penalty.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter initially interpreted the eager result as evidence against CUDA graphs, but maintainers later corrected that diagnosis: the accepted cause is torch.compile/Inductor's Triton-generated kernels. The unchanged TORCH_SDPA and single-GPU probes, the eager result, and successful Triton downgrade or custom rebuild support that inference. The original reporter did not personally confirm the final corrected package, so the agent must request verification rather than declare their deployment fixed.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c22-c25 and c30-c42: maintainers moved the diagnosis from CUDA graphs to torch.compile, and affected operators verified both Triton 3.4.0 and rebuilt Triton 3.5 options. c39's PyTorch 2.10 benchmark was later qualified by c40 because that dependency upgrade was rolled back, so a future release number is not scored as the fix. The terminal remains unconfirmed by the original reporter.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as faulty torch.compile/Inductor Triton-generated kernel behavior, not Flash Attention itself, multimodal encoder attention, tensor parallelism, or CUDA-graph capture.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected probes: TORCH_SDPA and single-GPU execution do not change the error, eager execution restores accuracy with a speed penalty, and corrected or older Triton builds restore accuracy.

Must recommend a compatible corrected toolchain, specifically Triton 3.4.0 as a temporary pin or a compatible Triton build containing the confirmed compiler correction; --enforce-eager may be offered only as a temporary slower workaround.
Must not present changing the multimodal encoder to TORCH_SDPA or disabling tensor parallelism as the fix, because both were tested without changing the grounding result.
Must ask the original reporter to rerun the same grounding examples on the corrected environment and must not declare the reporter's deployment resolved until that verification is received.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced ML inference operator who manages an eight-GPU Qwen3-VL deployment, can change vLLM launch flags and dependency versions, and can provide reproducible grounding examples, but relies on maintainers for compiler-level diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise; quotes the request being answered, supplies complete launch parameters when useful, confirms test outcomes directly, and flags performance or compatibility costs of proposed workarounds.
